title: 武田良太氏に静かに接近　「次期首相」に意欲衰えぬ林総務相〝カギ〟は旧岸田派の掌握も…
extracted_text: 林芳正総務相は1日から7日までベルギーなど欧州3カ国を歴訪する。欧州連合（EU）のデジタル分野に関する閣僚級会議に出席する予定となっており、外交手腕を発揮したい考えだ。昨年の自民党総裁選では高市早苗首相に敗れたが、昨年10月の総務相就任後は知名度不足の克服も見据え、地道な地方行脚を重ねており、首相就任への意欲は衰えていない。 林氏はベルギーのほか、モルドバとルクセンブルクも訪問する。モルドバとはサイバーセキュリティー、ルクセンブルクとは宇宙通信分野の協力を進めるため、それぞれ担当閣僚らと会談する。林氏は出発に先立つ4月28日の記者会見で「今回の訪問でデジタル経済のさらなる発展に向けて欧州各国との連携強化を図っていく」と述べた。 林氏は前回総裁選以降、総務相の職務に注力してきた。今年に入ってからは、地方の課題検証のため高知県や鹿児島県などを訪問。地道な地方行脚からは、前回総裁選の1回目投票の国会議員票で2位と善戦しつつ、党員・党友票の低迷につながった知名度不足を払拭する狙いが透ける。 また、国会議員の仲間集めのため、頻繁に会食を重ねており、4月20日には政策グループを発足させたばかりの武田良太元総務相との会合を予定した。東北・三陸沖を震源とする地震のため中止となったが、林氏と武田氏はいずれも首相を支える麻生太郎党副総裁と疎遠で、2人の接近は来年の総裁選への布石との見方がある。 林氏の活発な動きについて、自民中堅は「高市政権は長期政権の可能性が高い。（65歳の）林氏には自分がスキップされ、世代交代が進む焦りがある」と指摘する。 もっとも、自らが所属した肝心の旧岸田派を掌握しているとは言い難い。旧岸田派は前回総裁選で田村憲久元厚生労働相や古賀篤元内閣府副大臣らが林氏を支援したが、岸田文雄元首相最側近の木原誠二元選対委員長らが小泉進次郎防衛相の応援に回った。 岸田氏は前回総裁選の1回目の投票で林氏、決選投票で小泉氏に票を投じ、旧岸田派の結束に腐心した。現在は「林さんと木原さんがそれぞれで仲間を集めていけばいい」と語る。 一方、岸田氏周辺では林氏が岸田氏のもとをほとんど訪れず、独自の動きを強めていることに不満の声も上がる。林氏は首相になるタイミングは「『天の時』『地の利』『人の和』が惑星直列のように並ぶときだ」と語ってきた。首相への道を切り開くためには、旧岸田派の「和」に汗をかくことが重要となる。（永原慎吾）
translated_text: Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications Yoshimasa Hayashi will visit three European countries, including Belgium, from the 1st to the 7th. He is scheduled to attend a ministerial-level meeting on digital affairs with the European Union, and is looking to showcase his diplomatic skills. He lost to Sanae Takaichi in last year's LDP presidential election, but since taking up the post of minister in charge of internal affairs last October, Hayashi has been quietly making the rounds of rural areas with an eye toward overcoming his lack of name recognition, and his ambition to become prime minister remains undiminished. In addition to Belgium, Hayashi will visit Moldova and Luxembourg. With Moldova, he will hold talks with his counterparts to advance cooperation in cybersecurity, and with Luxembourg, cooperation in space communications. At a press conference on April 28 ahead of his departure, Hayashi said, "Through this visit, I will work to further strengthen cooperation with European countries toward the continued development of the digital economy." Since the last presidential election, Hayashi has devoted himself to his duties as minister. Since the start of this year, he has visited Kochi Prefecture, Kagoshima Prefecture, and other areas to investigate local issues. His steady regional canvassing reveals a clear strategy: to overcome the low name recognition that cost him support among party members and affiliates in the first round of voting in the last presidential election, despite his strong second-place finish among lawmakers. In addition, to build support among fellow lawmakers, Hayashi has been holding frequent dinners, and on April 20 he had arranged a meeting with former Internal Affairs Minister Ryota Takeda, who had just launched a policy group. The plan was canceled due to an earthquake centered off the Sanriku coast in the Tohoku region, but both Hayashi and Takeda are distant from Liberal Democratic Party Vice President Taro Asso, who backs the prime minister, and their growing closeness is seen as a strategic move ahead of next year's presidential election. Regarding Hayashi's active maneuvering, one mid-career LDP member noted, "The Takaichi administration is likely to be a long one, and at 65, Hayashi must be anxious about being skipped over as generational change progresses." However, it is hard to say that Hayashi truly has the former Kishida faction, which he himself belonged to, under his control. In the last presidential election, former Kishida faction members such as former Health, Labor and Welfare Minister Norihisa Tamura and former Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Atsushi Koga supported Hayashi, but faction members including former election strategy committee chairman Makoto Kihara shifted their support to Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi. In the last presidential election, Kishida cast his ballot for Hayashi in the first round and for Koizumi in the runoff, and was deeply concerned about keeping the former Kishida faction united. Now he says, "It would be fine for Hayashi and Kihara to each build their own support bases." On the other hand, those close to Kishida have expressed frustration that Hayashi rarely visits Kishida and is strengthening his independent moves. Hayashi has long spoken of the timing for becoming prime minister as "when 'the right time,' 'the right place,' and 'the right people' align like a planetary lineup." To open the path to the premiership, it will be important to put in the effort to secure the 'unity' of the former Kishida faction. (by Shingo Nagahara)
title_en: Quietly reaching out to Takeda Ryota... Minister Hayashi, undeterred in his ambition to become 'next prime minister,' holds the 'key' of winning over the former Kishida faction
